request.prompt: A brand-new hero-elevation BGM written the way today's big Tamil and Telugu film composers write a mass hero's entry theme, played with a futuristic cyberpunk sound. Instrumental, no lyrics. South Indian film style in the writing: a raga-shaped hook in B minor with chromatic notes, fast ornamented turns, bends and slides on every lead; the swinging Tamil mass bounce; full-band stop-and-slam hits; a wordless male crowd chant answering the hook. About 99 BPM, dark and mysterious at first, then heavy and proud. Keep it fresh: every 10 seconds the hook moves to a NEW lead sound and something new joins, never the same sound twice in a row. Timeline: 0-8 s: one deep boom, then a bent synth lead alone plays a rising three-note call and the hook over a soft dark arpeggio. 8-18 s: the hook moves to a bright plucked synth like a glitchy veena; a deep pulsing bass enters. 18-28 s: the mass groove slams in with heavy drums; the hook moves to a distorted electric guitar with bends; the crowd chant answers it. 28-38 s: the hook moves to huge brass stabs; a fast rolling triplet percussion pattern and a soaring string counter-melody join. 38-48 s: the band stops dead for one beat; then a sharp hero whistle plays a new variation of the hook over a slow half-time stomp, and a double-time triplet drum build rises. 48-60 s: the biggest section: the hook lifted up a whole step, synth lead, guitar and brass trading it phrase by phrase with the crowd chant; the ending is a rhythmic phrase played three times that lands hard on the final downbeat, then the three-note call alone. Not Western pop, not Hollywood trailer music, not plain synthwave, not EDM, no white-noise risers, no side-chain pumping, not ambient, no long repeats of the same sound.
